about: The consecration of the chalice, and the command to repeat it. The words over the chalice are longer than any biblical account: mystérium fídei stands in no narrative of the institution, and ætérni is the Canon's addition to the new covenant of Lk 22 and 1 Cor 11 — the phrase blood of the eternal covenant itself comes from Heb 13:20. The sentence Hæc quotiescúmque fecéritis is a quotation from 1 Cor 11.

s02.translation: In like manner, when supper was ended,

s03.narrative: The priest takes the chalice in both hands.

s04.translation: taking also this excellent chalice into his holy and venerable hands, again giving thanks to thee, he blessed and gave to his disciples, saying:

s05.translation: Take and drink of it, all of you.

s06.narrative: The priest speaks the words of consecration over the chalice attentively, without break and silently, holding it slightly raised.

s07.translation: For this is the Chalice of my Blood, of the new and eternal covenant: the mystery of faith: which shall be shed for you and for many unto the remission of sins.

s08.narrative: The words spoken, the priest sets the chalice on the corporal and says silently:

s09.translation: As often as you shall do these things, you shall do them in memory of me.

s10.narrative: The priest genuflects and adores, rises, shows the chalice to the people, sets it down, covers it and genuflects again.

w001.function: Símili modo, an ablative of manner; two words standing in the Canon for everything that passed between the one consecration and the other.

w004.function: Cenátum est has no subject: literally it has been dined. The dictionaries head cenátum as an adjective and it is tagged so here, but strictly it is the impersonal passive of ceno.

w006.function: A present participle with a perfect verb: an action going on at the same time as the blessing.

w009.function: Literally very bright; the præ- intensifies rather than meaning before.

w010.function: A calix is an ordinary Roman wine cup; Latin has no capital letter for it — the missal printers supply one.

w017.function: Item — likewise: it marks the gesture as a repetition of what was done with the bread.

w022.function: Over the chalice there is no fregit: the breaking belonged to the bread.

w030.function: The pronoun points to the chalice; ex eo, out of it, where the bread had ex hoc, of this.

w038.function: A genitive agreeing with “testaménti” (w041), not with “Sánguinis” (w036).

w040.function: Eternal stands in no account of the institution; the phrase blood of the eternal covenant comes from Hebrews.

w041.function: A Roman testamentum is a disposition made against one's death; biblical Latin used the word for the Hebrew covenant, and both senses sound here.

w042.function: Nominative: in apposition to “Calix” (w035), governed by nothing. These two words stand in no account of the institution.

w044.function: Masculine, because the relative agrees with “Calix” (w035) and not with the blood; English cannot show the difference.

w050.function: Future, not past: at the moment of the Supper the blood had not yet been shed.

w056.function: A future perfect: an action complete before the one “faciétis” (w060) names. The same form can be a perfect subjunctive, and the future that follows decides it.

w058.function: The genitive of the personal pronoun, not the possessive adjective: memory of me, not my memory.
